title: Measuring Sociality in Driving Interaction
reasoning: The paper extensively discusses 'sociality,' 'social preferences,' 'implicit social norms,' 'courtesy and respect,' and aims to design autonomous vehicles (AVs) that exhibit 'socially preferable' and 'human-like' behaviors in driving interactions. This involves integrating implicit moral and social rules observed in human drivers. It also evaluates if certain competitive behaviors are 'necessary or beneficial' in the context of human-AV interaction, directly touching upon ethical considerations for AV design.
